cases.explain: «девятого часа» — after the preposition «около», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”

cases.sentence: Он ясно видел ___, который явился ему и сказал:
cases.explain: «Божьего ангела» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”

cases.sentence: Когда ангел, говоривший с ним, ушел, Корнилий позвал двух своих слуг и благочестивого солдата, исполнявшего его ___.
cases.explain: «личные поручения» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When the angel who spoke to him had departed, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.

cases.sentence: В полдень ___, когда посланные уже подходили к городу, Петр поднялся на крышу дома помолиться .
cases.explain: «следующего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Now on the next day as they were on their journey, and got close to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.

cases.sentence: В этом полотне были всякие виды ___, пресмыкающиеся и птицы.
cases.explain: «четвероногих животных» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.

cases.explain: «второй раз» — after the preposition «во», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: A voice came to him again the second time, “What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”

cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On the next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and his near friends.
